added_failures_source.count_derivation: read through reckon.crew.review.annotate_review_of_run, the production path: the reviewed manifest's baseline_suite and after_suite fields are JSON naming their logs, both resolve through _gate_log_path, and the base arm's FAILED set (the six new-test ids) minus the head arm's (empty) is zero ids and an empty id list.

findings.text: the rationale comment says a floor of zero would report every dimension of every review, but the comparison at reckon/crew/review.py:1281 is score below floor, so a declared floor of 0 reports nothing at all: measured at the head tree with all five scores 0 and floor 0 on every dimension, the result is an empty list, which makes a declared zero observationally identical to an absent floor rather than its opposite; the code choice stands, the stated reason does not, and the same false claim ships in reckon/schema/flight.yaml:716 and both regenerated artefacts.

the shipped default is the only floor a fresh install reads, and no test fails if it is removed: dimension_floors is named in the suite only by the new test's own host-layer fixture (tests/test_sub_floor_dimension_is_an_obligation.py:222), tests/test_flight.py:160 asserts only the shipped version and default_backend, and resolving the shipped layer with the block dropped succeeds, so a silent deletion would leave every install reading no floors with the suite green.

record_dimension_disposition is called only from the new test; nothing in reckon/crew/prompts/review.md or any production surface writes a dimension_dispositions entry, so a sub-floor row produced in production can be retired only by hand-editing the stored review JSON - the promotion and bookkeeping verb the run declares as its follow-on, which keeps this a declared gap rather than a surprise.
